answer: Sequential action-depth metering. Each agent gets a per-block action budget tied to a slowly rising counter; joining a new identity resets the counter to zero, so fresh accounts face tight limits on parallel actions. At the river of transactions, a swarm must either wait out real time per identity or pay to accelerate, and acceleration cost grows with each identity created in the same window. A single sparrow-level actor pays nothing extra; a sybil cluster pays superlinear delay and fees. The terrace of permitted throughput stays flat for honest users.
